p: faith is the substance of things: An excellent description of faith by the effects, because it represents things which are but yet in hope, and sets as it were before our eyes things that are invisible.
For by it the: He shows that the fathers ought to be accounted of by this virtue.
elders obtained a good report: That is, those fathers from whom we came: and whose authority and example ought to move us very much.
Through faith we understand that the: He shows the property of faith, by setting before us most cautious examples of those who from the beginning of the world excelled in the Church.
seen were not made of things: So that the world which we see, was not made from any matter that appeared or was before, but from nothing.
By faith Abel offered unto God: Abel.
By faith Enoch was translated that: Enoch.
see death: That he should not die.
rewarder of them that diligently seek: This reward is not referred to our merits, but to the free promise, as Paul teaches in Abraham the father of all the faithful, Ro 4:4.
By faith Noah: Noah.
By faith Abraham: Abraham and Sarah.
foundations: This foundation is contrasted with their tabernacle.
dead: As unlikely to bear children, as if he had been dead.
faith: In faith, which they had while they lived, and followed, them even to their grave.
promises: This is the figure metonymy, for the things promised.
embraced them: For the patriarchs were given to profess their religion by building an altar and calling on the name of the Lord when they received the promises.
tried: Tried by the Lord.
promises offered up his only begotten: Although the promises of life were made in that only begotten son Isaac, yet he appointed him to die; and so against hope he believed in hope.
whence also he received him in: From which death.
a figure: For there was not the true and very death of Isaac, but as it were the death, by means of which he seemed also to have risen again.
By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and: Isaac.
By faith Jacob: Jacob.
By faith Joseph: Joseph.
By faith Moses: Moses.
pleasures of sin for a season: Such pleasures as he could not enjoy, unless he provoked God's wrath against him.
By faith they passed through the: The Red Sea.
By faith the walls of Jericho: Jericho.
By faith the: Rahab.
harlot Rahab perished not with them: A notable example of God's goodness.
spies with peace: Courteously and friendly, so that not only did she not hurt them, but also kept them safe.
And what shall I more say: Gideon, Barak and other judges and prophets.
promises: The fruit of the promises.
Women received their dead raised to: He seems to mean the story of that woman of Sarepta, whose son Elijah raised again from the dead, and the Shunammite, whose son Elisha restored to his mother.
tortured: He means that perfection which Antiochus wrought.
sheepskins and goatskins: In vile and rough clothing, so were the saints brought to extreme poverty, and constrained to live like beasts in the wilderness.

And these all: An amplification taken from the circumstance of the time: their faith is so much the more to be marvelled at, by how much the promises of things to come were more dark, yet at length were indeed exhibited to us, so that their faith and ours is as one, as is also their consecration and ours.
not the promise: But saw Christ afar off.
without us should not be made: For their salvation depended on Christ, who was exhibited in our days.
